comments.content: The closing brace and next declaration are on the same line. This is malformed formatting and may fail the repository's style/format checks; put `ClearAudioCache` on its own line.

With differential scrolling, every frame scans all not-yet-spawned notes, and each eligible removal shifts the remaining list. A chart with many notes can therefore incur quadratic total shifting plus per-frame O(n) scans, causing avoidable frame spikes. Keep notes ordered by the threshold-crossing calculation or use a structure that removes eligible notes without shifting the entire remainder.

The 64 MiB input and PCM budgets are enforced independently, but this path keeps the complete FLAC byte array alive while the decoder builds its PCM output (and then stores that output in the audio stream/cache). Peak memory can therefore exceed either individual budget substantially. Consider accounting for combined peak memory or lowering the per-buffer limits for this runtime path.

The LPC dot product can exceed `long` (up to 32 signed 32-bit coefficients multiplied by 24-bit samples), and the unchecked accumulation/narrowing then silently wraps malformed input into bogus PCM. Use checked accumulation or a wider/saturating strategy and reject values outside the supported sample/residual range before narrowing.

The UTF-8-style FLAC frame/sample number encoder does not mask the payload to the lead byte's available bits. For values needing two or more continuation bytes, the high payload bits can set prefix bits and corrupt the encoded number. Current round-trip inputs do not exercise this because they remain below 128; add large-frame-number coverage and mask the payload (and verify the corresponding decoder behavior).

`GuiInput` events have positions local to this Control, while the release forwarded from `EditorPreviewController._Input` is viewport-relative. Feeding both through this conversion makes release coordinates incorrect whenever the stage Control is offset (and may end a drag at the wrong position). Convert global events to this Control's local coordinates before mapping, or avoid forwarding a second event path.

Exceptions thrown by the command handler are not generally contained here. For example, `load` can throw decoder/audio I/O exceptions, and `authoring` can throw from `Enum.Parse`; these are outside the catch filter and can escape `Drain` and terminate the preview process. Catch command-processing exceptions broadly and emit an error event (while still allowing fatal process errors to propagate if needed).

`Ended` is assigned by the background `ReadLoop` thread and polled by `_Process` on the Godot thread, but this property is not volatile and no lock/other synchronization protects the access. Mark the backing state volatile or use an explicit synchronization mechanism so EOF is reliably observed.
comments.existing_code: public bool Ended { get; private set; }

comments.content: A staged FLAC is read into one byte array sized directly from the file length, with no size budget. Large input can exhaust process memory before metadata or frame limits are checked. Parse incrementally or enforce a documented maximum input size before allocating.
comments.existing_code:
var bytes = new byte[length];
        AudioProbeSupport.ReadExactlyAt(stream, 0, bytes, source, "truncated FLAC file");

comments.content: This scan accepts any later CRC-valid header, regardless of whether the bytes between it and the prior header form a valid frame. Corrupt/truncated payloads with a planted header and a matching summed block size can therefore pass validation. Validate actual frame boundaries/payload (for example, via the FLAC frame decoder) rather than searching arbitrary payload bytes.
comments.existing_code:
var next = FindFrameHeader(bytes, headerEnd, info);
            if (next < 0)

comments.content: Chunk iteration is bounded by physical file length, but RIFF declares its own container size in header bytes 4–7. Bytes appended after that declared boundary can be interpreted as chunks and counted as audio, yielding an incorrect duration. Bound traversal to the declared RIFF end and reject chunks extending beyond it.

Returning as soon as STREAMINFO's sample count is reached silently accepts arbitrary trailing data, including malformed or additional audio frames. This also means the decoder never verifies that the remaining bytes are only permitted metadata/padding. Reject unexpected trailing bytes or explicitly parse supported trailing tags so appended corruption cannot be treated as a successfully decoded file.

if (streamInfo.TotalSamples > 0 && writer.WrittenFrames >= streamInfo.TotalSamples)
                return; // 已满足声明长度；尾随字节（多为标签/填充）不再解释为帧

comments.content: `frames * channels * 2` is evaluated as `int` and can overflow before array allocation, producing an unrelated allocation/argument exception for large test fixtures. Compute the byte length with checked arithmetic (or a wider type) so invalid sizes fail deterministically.

Trailing bytes are appended before final byte alignment. If the last frame ends mid-byte, these bytes become part of its padded frame data rather than bytes after the frame; current fixtures happen to use byte-aligned frames, but this helper should align before appending trailing data to reliably test trailing-byte handling.

Stage events feed their bar values directly into this conversion, but NaN, infinity, or sufficiently large finite values are not rejected before the floating-point-to-`long` cast. Such input can overflow into an invalid exact time and make placement/path commands fail (or behave unexpectedly); validate finiteness and a representable/allowed upper bound before converting.
comments.existing_code:
private static ExactBarTime ExactTime(double bar) =>
        ExactBarTime.FromFraction((long)Math.Round(Math.Max(0, bar) * 1_000_000d), 1_000_000);

comments.content: The shared localizer outlives each `InspectorView`, but this subscription is never removed. Closing and recreating workbench windows therefore keeps the old view (and its control tree) rooted and invokes `UpdateInspector` on it for every language change. Unsubscribe when the control is detached/disposed, or use a weak/event-lifetime pattern.

When a path-node selection is active, this displays `CurveToNext` for that node, but for a note selection with nodes it displays the note-level curve. Applying the curve command for the note may not affect the visible first segment once path nodes exist (the node curve takes precedence), so the UI can appear to accept a change without changing the rendered path. Consider resolving the first effective segment curve or disabling note-level editing when nodes are present.
